Same as 1, but the mean of the sex-level ALB averages is an unweighted mean across sexes (each sex counts equally), not weighted by patient count.

Same as 1, but the per-patient ratio is the ratio of the patient's average UN to the patient's average T-BIL, not the average of per-test ratios.

"How far its ALB average is above that mean" is the difference (sex ALB average minus mean of sex averages).
"How far its ALB average is above that mean" is a percentage or ratio relative to the mean.

Lab records are joined to patients by Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID with an inner join, so lab records with no matching patient are dropped. Patients with no lab records are also excluded.
The patient grouping key is (ID, SEX), so a patient with multiple SEX values (not possible given ID is the primary key) would form separate groups.
The output is one row per qualifying sex with columns sex, average ALB, average UN/T-BIL ratio, and the difference.
The output covers all qualifying sexes in a single result, with the mean of the sex-level ALB averages used only as a threshold and not shown as a column.
The ALB average ignores null ALB values, and the ratio average ignores null UN or null T-BIL values.
Patient-level averages are computed across all lab dates for each patient, with no date filter.

queries:
WITH patient_avg AS (
    SELECT P.ID, P.SEX,
           AVG(L.ALB) AS avg_alb,
           AVG(CAST(L.UN AS REAL) / NULLIF(L."T-BIL", 0)) AS avg_ratio
    FROM Patient P
    JOIN Laboratory L ON L.ID = P.ID
    GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX
),
sex_avg AS (
    SELECT SEX,
           AVG(avg_alb) AS sex_alb,
           AVG(avg_ratio) AS sex_ratio
    FROM patient_avg
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT SEX
FROM sex_avg
WHERE sex_alb > (SELECT AVG(sex_alb) FROM sex_avg);
SELECT AVG(avg_alb) FROM (SELECT AVG(L.ALB) AS avg_alb FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.SEX)
SELECT AVG(patient_alb) AS mean_alb
FROM (
    SELECT P.ID, AVG(L.ALB) AS patient_alb
    FROM Patient P
    JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID
    WHERE L.ALB IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY P.ID
);
SELECT ID, AVG(UN) * 1.0 / AVG(`T-BIL`) AS ratio
FROM Laboratory
GROUP BY ID
HAVING AVG(`T-BIL`) IS NOT NULL AND AVG(`T-BIL`) <> 0;
SELECT AVG(GOT * 1.0 / `T-BIL`) FROM Laboratory WHERE `T-BIL` IS NOT NULL AND `T-BIL` <> 0;
SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN "T-BIL" = 0 THEN NULL ELSE GOT * 1.0 / "T-BIL" END)
FROM Laboratory;
